headline: A strong storm is soaking Western Washington tonight into Thanksgiving with heavy rain, damaging gusts (up to 60 mph on the coast, 50 mph in the North Interior and San Juans, 45 mph around Puget Sound), heavy North Cascades snow, and coastal flooding at Thursday's high tides, including along the Strait from 10 AM to 6 PM.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Widespread rain is falling Wednesday evening, heaviest from the coast to the west side of Puget Sound; Hoquiam and Quillayute had already topped 1 inch by 5 PM and could see about another inch by midnight, while the eastern side of the Sound gets noticeably less. Winds keep strengthening overnight under Wind Advisories until noon Thursday for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including Sequim and Port Angeles), the Lake Crescent/US 101 area, Port Townsend, the San Juans, Whidbey Island, the North Interior and the Seattle, Eastside, Kitsap, Tacoma and Olympia areas, with gusts to about 50 mph in the North Interior and San Juans and 45 mph along Puget Sound; Seattle's strongest winds are expected from about 2 to 7 AM. The outer coast is under a High Wind Warning until noon Thursday with gusts up to 60 mph. In the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades, a Winter Storm Warning runs until 4 AM Friday, with 8 to 16 inches of snow possible, mostly tonight into Thursday, and snow levels around 5,000 to 6,000 feet (lower in the North Cascades Thursday morning).

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The front passes early Thanksgiving morning, and rain turns showery during the day as the air becomes unstable enough for scattered thunderstorms, with a 20 to 25 percent chance on the coast and Olympic Peninsula and about 15 percent or less elsewhere, including Seattle. Gusty winds continue Thursday as they shift to the southwest (Seattle gusts near 30 mph in the afternoon) before easing Thursday evening. Storm totals of an additional 2 to 4 inches through Thursday fall mostly on the Olympic Peninsula and coast; rivers will rise but widespread flooding isn't expected, except on the Skokomish River, which should peak at moderate flood stage late tonight into early Thursday and drop below flood stage Friday, and more small landslides are possible on the Bear Gulch burn scar on the Olympic Peninsula. A weaker system keeps rain chances going on Friday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Forecast models agree well that a weak area of high pressure builds over the Pacific Northwest late Friday and through the weekend, giving a break from the rain Saturday and Sunday. The stormy pattern returns next week, starting with another system Monday that brings breezy winds, mainly to the coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

coast: Coastal flooding remains the headline hazard as some of the year's highest tides combine with storm surge and high surf, with the worst inland-water impacts early Thursday before the tides gradually weaken. A Coastal Flood Warning runs 10 AM to 6 PM Thursday for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca (Sequim, Port Angeles) and the Washington coast, and 3 AM to 10 AM Thursday for Seattle, Everett, Shoreline/Lynnwood, eastern Kitsap, Island County, Hood Canal, Olympia/south Sound, the San Juans and the Pierce/south King, Skagit/Snohomish and Whatcom lowlands; Coastal Flood Advisories cover Port Townsend (3 to 10 AM Thursday) and the lower Chehalis River valley (10 AM to 6 PM Thursday). Coastal Flood Watches follow for the San Juans late Thursday night into Friday morning and for the Grays Harbor coast Friday morning through Friday evening. On the water, a Storm Warning covers the coastal waters and Gale Warnings cover the Strait entrances, Admiralty Inlet and the northern inland waters/San Juans until 10 AM Thursday, with a Gale Warning for Puget Sound and Hood Canal from midnight to 7 AM Thursday and Small Craft Advisories before and after (central Strait and Grays Harbor bar until 10 PM Thursday; coastal waters and west Strait 10 AM to 10 PM Thursday; Puget Sound and Hood Canal until midnight tonight and 7 AM to 7 PM Thursday). Thunderstorms over the coastal waters early Thursday may drift into the inland waters with lightning, gusty winds and small hail. Seas of 15 to 21 feet continue into Thursday, ease to 10 to 15 feet late Thursday into Friday and below 10 feet over the weekend (with a weak westerly push through the Strait late Saturday into Sunday), then climb above 10 feet again next week, when more advisories are likely.
watch_for: Thursday's high tides: 3–10 AM around Puget Sound, then 10 AM–6 PM along the Strait (Sequim/Port Angeles) and outer coast
Damaging gusts tonight into Thursday morning, strongest on the coast, North Interior and San Juans
Skokomish River flooding and possible landslides on the Bear Gulch burn scar through Thursday
confidence: Forecasters say the storm is on track tonight and Thursday, though exact rain totals east of Puget Sound and the timing of any Thursday thunderstorms are less certain; models agree well on the dry weekend, with few specifics yet on next week's storms.
